title: Can you ask AI bots to hack a website or a business?
content_md: People can certainly ask artificial intelligence (AI) bots to attack a targeted business or website. But most AI chat assistants politely reject these requests and refuse to help with cyberattacks. Mainstream chatbots have weaknesses, and attackers can sometimes trick them into providing advice on how to plan or carry out an attack. However, these chatbots cannot independently launch a cyberattack against a target. In contrast, autonomous AI agents can carry out attacks with minimal human supervision . And as AI technology advances, these attacks may become increasingly effective. Key Takeaways: Mainstream AI chatbots reject cyberattack requests, but malicious actors can bypass guardrails using creative prompts or jailbreaks. Autonomous AI agents can execute complex network breaches with minimal human instruction and oversight. Using AI tools to gain unauthorized access to computer systems is illegal and punishable under cybersecurity laws. AI systems lack legal personhood, making human operators fully responsible for crimes committed by autonomous agents.
